name: The Soft Audit
creator: Meridian Verified Media Group (HelixCorp subsidiary)
description: A prestige interview program in which prominent Tier 4 and Tier 5 executives, corponation architects, and civic leaders are interviewed in long-form conversations designed to present corporate leadership as thoughtful, humane, and philosophically engaged. Host Cassander Mwangi-Solis is a former investigative journalist whose questions are genuinely incisive but whose follow-ups are, by contractual arrangement, consistently gentle. The production values are immaculate — the show is engineered to feel like journalism while functioning as reputation management.
medium: premium neural feed / high-fidelity BCI audio with ambient sensory layer
cultural_impact: The Soft Audit has become the preeminent venue through which Meridian 88's corporate class constructs its public narrative, and its guest list functions as an unofficial index of who holds real power in the city; notably, the show has never featured a guest who was subsequently charged with a corporate crime, though several have been investigated after appearing.
controversy: Mwangi-Solis's 2208 interview with Vantara Group's Chief Continuity Officer — conducted three weeks before Vantara's Tier 2 housing complex collapse that killed 90 residents — was retroactively scrutinized for questions the host asked but did not pursue, reigniting debate about whether the show is journalism, PR, or something more deliberately deceptive.
story_hooks: An upcoming episode features an executive whose interview will serve as their alibi for a night during which something catastrophic is planned; the recording schedule is known, and someone needs to either stop the taping or use it.
Mwangi-Solis has kept private notes of every follow-up question he was contractually barred from asking over twelve years of episodes — and he wants someone to help him decide what to do with them.
A guest has agreed to appear on The Soft Audit specifically to deliver a coded message to a specific listener; the production team has no idea, but someone in the city's intelligence apparatus does.
